short_description: The middle fibre of the three human skeletal muscle types: fast like Type IIx, but with enough mitochondria and myoglobin to also run oxidatively, giving it noticeably better fatigue resistance than its purely glycolytic sibling. A single, unbranched, cylindrical multinucleated cell centimetres long (~30 mm) and ~60 um across -- narrower than Type IIx, wider than Type I -- cross-striated by regular transverse A/I banding along its whole length, with many flattened nuclei just under the sarcolemma at the periphery (never one central nucleus), a moderate density of mitochondria and a moderate surrounding capillary network, and a pale rose-pink colour between Type I's deep red and Type IIx's near-white cream.
